stocks.name: Godrej Agrovet Ltd
stocks.fundamental: Diversified agri-business (animal feed, crop protection, oil palm, dairy, foods). Q1 FY27 is a case of good top line, weak bottom line: consolidated sales +10% to ₹2,852cr but EBITDA −9% to ₹255cr, margin compressing to 8.9% from 10.8%, and PAT −14% to ₹128cr. Animal Nutrition was the bright spot — cattle feed volumes +15%, segment result +36% — and Oil Palm revenue +28.9% on better CPO realisations and an improved 18.8% extraction ratio. Crop Care fell 17.2% on a delayed monsoon. Genuine positives: net working capital days improved to 21 from 31, ROCE ~20%, Astec reached EBITDA breakeven, ICRA reaffirmed AA/A1+, and India's first integrated oil palm complex opened in Telangana. Watch items: CFO transition (S. Varadaraj superannuating, Ravishankar A. from 1 Oct), and management deferring precise FY27 guidance until after Q2. The stock fell ~4% on results despite a slight EPS beat.

stocks.name: Castrol India Limited
stocks.fundamental: Near debt-free lubricants leader, 51% owned by bp; ~43% ROE, ~4.7% dividend yield, 109% payout. Q2 CY26 (Jun quarter) was excellent: revenue +25% to ₹1,871cr, PAT +43% to ₹348cr, EBITDA +41% to ₹494cr, interim dividend of ₹6.25 nearly doubled YoY. Two caveats. Management itself flagged that part of the margin came from consuming cheaper inventory carried from an earlier peak — a one-off, though they say profitability grew healthily even excluding it — and stayed cautious on H2 given commodity inflation and an uneven monsoon. Separately, bp is selling 65% of Castrol's global lubricants business to Stonepeak (~USD 10bn EV), expected to close end-2026; no financial impact yet, but the ownership change is a live overhang. Stock is down ~9% over a year despite the earnings, and trades ~9.7x book.

stocks.name: Jubilant Foodworks Limited
stocks.fundamental: Operates Domino's, Popeyes and Hong's Kitchen; 3,712 stores. Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue +14.1% to ₹2,570cr but PAT only +6% to ₹100cr, EBITDA margin flat at 19.6%. The split matters more than the headline: Popeyes like-for-like sales grew 45% (third straight quarter above 40%, revenue +97%), while core Domino's India LFL was just 2.5% against 11.6% a year ago. So growth is coming from a small, fast brand while the large mature one has stalled. Management guides 5-7% Domino's LFL for FY27 with recovery from Q2. Broker views diverge sharply — Jefferies Buy at ₹650, HSBC Hold at ₹500. Debt-to-equity 0.76, capex ₹750-900cr, and the stock trades near 88x against a sector ~62x. Expensive for the growth currently being delivered.

stocks.name: Life Insurance Corporation of India Ltd
stocks.fundamental: India's largest life insurer and the cleanest fundamental story in this week's list. Q1 FY27 PAT +22.8% to ₹13,492cr, but the more meaningful number is Value of New Business +61.3% to ₹3,136cr with VNB margin expanding 750bps to 22.9% from 15.4%. That reflects a real mix shift — non-par products now 32.5% of individual APE versus 30.3% a year ago, with non-par savings APE +59% and protection +44%. Solvency improved to 2.42 from 2.17; AUM ₹59.4 lakh crore. Three honest caveats: headline growth is modest (total APE only +8.2%, premium +6.75%, and policies sold up just 2.1%), so profit is coming from margin not volume; first-year premium market share slipped to 60.10% from 63.51% as private competition bites; and 61st-month persistency weakened to 61.12% from 63.85%.

stocks.name: Hindustan Oil Exploration Company Limited
stocks.fundamental: Small Chennai-based oil and gas explorer (~₹2,060cr market cap). Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41-45% YoY to ₹124cr consolidated, but profit collapsed: standalone PAT −74% to ₹12.5cr and consolidated net profit down to ₹6.2cr from ₹43.9cr. Worse, standalone other income of ₹19.4cr included one-offs — an ₹8cr escrow release and a ₹2cr insurance claim — meaning operating profit was thinner still. Operationally B-80 produced only 605 BOEPD and a dispute with HPCL over a ~417,000-barrel cargo containing organic chlorides is unresolved, with the oil being resold to third parties into late 2026. Dirok and Kharsang are improving, and FY27 capex is USD 45mn with three new B-80 wells in Q4. Also note: the company was fined by both exchanges for delayed FY26 results amid management and auditor changes, pays no dividend despite repeated profits, and Screener flags a low tax rate. Genuinely high-risk.

stocks.name: V-guard Industries Limited
stocks.fundamental: Kochi-based electricals and consumer durables (stabilisers, water heaters, wires, kitchen appliances). Excellent quarter: Q1 FY27 revenue +23.5% to ₹1,811cr against 14-15% full-year guidance, PAT +76% to ₹130cr, EBITDA margin up 210bps to 10.5%. Net cash improved sharply to ₹670cr from ₹155cr. Growth was helped by a favourable summer and pricing actions that offset copper inflation, so some of this is seasonal rather than run-rate. South region grew 36.7% vs 12% non-South.

stocks.name: Deepak Nitrite Limited
stocks.fundamental: Specialty chemicals — phenolics and advanced intermediates. Best quarter on record: Q1 FY27 revenue +35% to ₹2,592cr, PAT +207% to ₹345cr, EBITDA margin doubling to 21% from 11%. Phenolics did the heavy lifting with record segment EBIT of ₹418cr at 24% margins. Debt-to-equity a comfortable 0.27x, and the board approved ₹2,500cr for a 240 KTA Bisphenol A plant to deepen integration. Caveat: this is a cyclical spread business — the margin doubling reflects favourable phenol-benzene spreads as much as execution, and advanced intermediates still faces raw-material pressure.

stocks.name: Adani Ports And Special Economic Zone Limited
Balu Forge Industries Ltd
stocks.fundamental: Belgaum-based precision forging and machining, pivoting hard into defence and aerospace. Q1 FY27 revenue +29% to ₹300.7cr and PAT +15.9% to ₹66.1cr, with sequential revenue +14%. Strategically busy: maiden US aerospace order from Alpha Aircraft Systems, a five-year MoU with a NATO-affiliated entity for large-calibre shells, a ₹100cr confirmed order for 155mm ERFB shells, and an ICRA upgrade to A-(Stable)/A2+. The caution is in the margin trend and the funding. EBITDA margin fell to 28.2% from 31.0% and PAT margin to 21.7% from 24.3%, because finance costs more than doubled to ₹46cr and depreciation rose 96.5%. The board has approved a USD 60mn FCCB issue and a borrowing-limit increase to ₹1,000cr (EGM 4 Sept) — meaningful dilution and leverage ahead. Auditors also flagged a related-party property purchase and ongoing tax proceedings, and promoter holding fell 0.88% in the quarter. Note that some outlets misreport the figures in millions as crore; revenue is ₹300.7cr, not ₹3,007cr.

stocks.name: Shree Renuka Sugars Limited
stocks.fundamental: Wilmar-controlled sugar and ethanol producer, and the weakest balance sheet on either list — flag this one hard. Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹2,120cr (+5.5%) with a consolidated net loss of ₹252cr, only marginally better than the ₹260cr loss a year ago; the standalone loss actually widened slightly. The structural problem: standalone net worth is **negative ₹1,494cr**, consolidated current liabilities exceed current assets by roughly ₹3,691cr, and debt is around ₹5,566cr. FY26 closed with a ₹792cr net loss. Solvency rests on parent Wilmar International's continued liquidity support. The distillery segment is the one bright spot (revenue up sharply to ₹474cr) and India's ethanol blending push is a real tailwind, but this is a turnaround bet dependent on policy and a parent's balance sheet, not a compounding business. Peers like Balrampur Chini are far better capitalised.

stocks.name: Seamec Limited
stocks.fundamental: Offshore marine services — diving support vessels and vessel charter for oil and gas. Market cap ~₹4,159cr, up strongly over the past year; trailing revenue ₹952cr and profit ₹254cr, promoter holding 72.7%. Recent developments: a USD 9.42mn diving agreement with HAL Offshore, and vessel SEAMEC SWORDFISH off-hired from 30 July for planned maintenance, which will dent the coming quarter's utilisation. Caution: reported quarterly figures differ materially across secondary sources for this name — verify against the company filing before relying on any single quarter. Trades at roughly 3x book and the effective tax rate looks unusually low. Revenue is inherently lumpy since it depends on vessel day-rates and contract timing rather than a steady order book.

stocks.name: Max Estates Ltd
stocks.fundamental: NCR real-estate developer (Noida and Gurugram), wellbeing-led LiveWell/WorkWell positioning. The headline is pre-sales: ~₹1,093cr in Q1 FY27, over 5x YoY, with 487 units sold against 43 a year ago, and ₹491cr collected. ICRA assigned a first-time A+ issuer rating. Commercial portfolio is 100% leased generating ₹150cr+ annual rent. But reported P&L is thin and going the other way — Q1 FY27 PAT fell 30% YoY to ₹8.35cr on revenue of ₹52cr, with EBITDA down 42%. That gap is normal for developers, where pre-sales convert to revenue only on construction milestones, but it means the accounts will lag the story for several quarters. GDV pipeline ₹16,150cr+.
